papers.instruction: Attempt three questions, question one is compulsory.

questions.text: Explain 'resurrection' and the stages.
questions.correctAnswer: Resurrection is the raising of the dead to life by the power of God. Its stages are: first, the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the firstfruits; second, the resurrection of the righteous dead at His coming; third, the resurrection of the wicked unto judgement.

questions.text: There are no 'superior' or 'insignificant' areas of service. Jesus measured greatness in terms of service, not 'status'. Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus measured greatness by service rather than status. Every area of service carries equal value before God; no role is superior or insignificant. Greatness in the kingdom is measured by faithful service, not by position, title or recognition.

questions.text: A Christian's 'servant's heart' is one major thing that reveals his/her Christian maturity. Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: A servant's heart reveals maturity because it puts others before self, mirrors Christ who came to serve and not to be served, and produces humility, availability and a willingness to serve without seeking recognition.

questions.text: If you don't use your gifts, abilities, endowments, etc. to serve, others get 'cheated'; if others don't use theirs, you get 'cheated'. Everyone is expected to play his part. Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: Gifts are given for the common good of the body of Christ. When one member fails to serve, others are deprived of what God intended for them through that member; when every member serves, the whole body benefits. Each believer is expected to play his or her part.

questions.text: God is not particular about the 'magnitude' of our responsibility but the degree of faithfulness. It is our 'fruitfulness' (output) that counts, not our title, position or 'office'. The way we sow (even in stewardship) is the same way we will reap. Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: God assesses faithfulness rather than the size of the responsibility, and fruitfulness rather than title, position or office. Because we reap what we sow, the manner of our sowing in stewardship determines the reward we receive.

papers.instruction: Attempt three questions, question five is compulsory.

questions.text: You can retire from your career, but you cannot 'retire' from serving God! Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: Career service ends at retirement, but Christian service is lifelong. A believer remains in service to God until death; there is no retirement from the Lord's work, only a change of assignment.

questions.text: Discipleship involves learning of Christ with the purpose of obeying Him totally. Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: Discipleship is learning from Christ as an apprentice with the aim of total obedience. It is continuous, demands commitment and concentration, and is proven by obedience rather than by knowledge alone.

questions.text: Every Christian is not called to be a pastor, but every Christian is called to Christian service. God wants to express his power, love and grace through us. Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: Not every believer is called to pastoral office, but every believer is called to service. Service is not optional; God desires to express His power, love and grace through the service of every Christian.

questions.text: 'I know of no more encouraging fact than the unquestionable ability of man to elevate his life by conscious endeavor.' Explain.
questions.correctAnswer: The statement stresses personal responsibility and deliberate effort. A person can lift his life by conscious endeavour rather than by passively reacting to circumstances, which is the difference between a reactive and a proactive life.

questions.text: Explain the terms: 'Hired workers', 'Servant workers' and 'Slave workers'.
questions.correctAnswer: Hired workers serve for reward and may abandon the work when it becomes inconvenient; servant workers serve dutifully but within limits; slave workers belong wholly to the master and serve without reserve, which is the highest level of service.
